This game is fascinating.

Story-wise, it's great. Very self aware. It pokes fun at the beautifully insane writing of Hideo Kojima, subverts your expectations and is sure to get a few laughs. Best enjoyed while streaming, or with some friends, for sure. 

Gameplay wise, it's quite rough around the edges. Controls are competent and explained well enough, but the stealth mechanics can be inconsistent and the Difficulty ranges from "Fisher Price Toy" to "Playing Five Finger Fillet with a chainsaw." I would say that at least two of the levels in [spoiler] Potato Tower [/spoiler] qualify this game for being a Torture Platformer.

That said, despite being rough, I didn't come across any game breaking bugs. This is clearly a game which had a lot of work and passion put into it, and I'm certainly looking forward to what Samer Khatib puts out next!

For the price of a cup of coffee, this game's a bargain and well worth playing in a Discord call with some friends.

Potato Man is an absolute masterpiece that takes players on a gastronomic journey like no other. From the very moment you step into the crispy world of this deep-fried delight, you're in for a treat that transcends the boundaries of conventional gaming.

The game's graphics are as golden and crispy as a perfectly fried potato, with a charming 2D aesthetic that immediately captures your attention. The attention to detail in Potato Man's pixelated universe is commendable, creating a visually appetizing experience that is both nostalgic and fresh.

The storyline is where Potato Man truly shines. Embark on a culinary odyssey as the titular character, navigating through a world filled with savory challenges and unexpected twists. The narrative unfolds with a perfect blend of humor and suspense, keeping players engaged and hungry for more. Each level is a unique dish in the grand feast of Potato Man's adventure, and the variety of settings and characters add layers to the already delicious storyline.

One cannot talk about Potato Man without mentioning the innovative deep-frying mechanic. Getting deep-fried is not just a punishment in this game; it's an experience! The way the developers have seamlessly integrated this element into the gameplay is nothing short of genius. The sizzle and crisp sound effects, combined with the temporary change in Potato Man's appearance, make for a memorable gaming moment. It adds a challenging twist to the traditional platformer genre, keeping players on their toes (or should I say, crispy edges).

The soundtrack deserves a special mention, perfectly complementing the game's quirky atmosphere. From the upbeat frying pan percussion to the melodic hum of the potato-themed background music, the audio enhances the overall immersive experience.

In conclusion, Potato Man is a culinary masterpiece that not only satisfies your gaming appetite but also leaves you craving for more. The deep-frying mechanic, coupled with the engaging storyline and delightful aesthetics, makes Potato Man a must-play for any gaming connoisseur. Prepare to be deep-fried and delighted in this whimsical journey through the world of spuds and surprises!

This game is like my ex, it just keeps coming back over and over, begging me to give it one more chance. And like the understanding, patient, deluded person I am, I just can't say no. I know what's waiting on the other side but I just can't stop myself from trying one more time. Because this time it's going to be different. This time I know that my robot son will understand that I'm a caring father that takes him to hunt down a serial killer because I just want to spend time with him. This time I will have the common decency to lock the door while I'm sitting on that toilet taking a dump. I expect so much, and it starts out so wonderful. And even though I know how it's going to end, I still love it. I'll never leave you Potato Thriller, you're the only one for me, you truly understand me and what I need in a game.

I'm not going to lie to you, this is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fever dream. Everything about this game is odd and janky. The controls suck and the gameplay is... something. There is no way in hell that I should have enjoyed this game. 

Needless to say, I enjoyed it. 

There's something cathartic about being able to say that you were able to complete a game that you've wanted to play for years, and this game encapsulates that feeling perfectly. I first saw this game on a YouTube channel about 4-5 years back. I watched the whole series as it came out and thought, "Huh, that looks funny. I should play it." I then realized that I was broke and couldn't buy it.
4 years later, and here we are. P.T. is a game that has haunted me for a large portion of my life, simply because it lived rent-free in my mind, begging me to play it one day. When I did, saying it was better than I expected would be an overstatement. It was Potato Thriller, and it would continue to be Potato Thriller until the end of time. 

Listen. I'm in doubt that there will ever a person who fully reads this review, but if you do, make of this game what you will. Its cut and dry, not anything more than it needs to be, and I think that's alright. There's nothing wrong with being simple, and sometimes basic is exactly what you need.
